text:
maya: Heads up — thinking about admin/gateway API for internal tooling. We need to settle: keep REST only or support gRPC as well? Looking at rollout + telemetry implications. /cc @sam @leo
sam: +1 to supporting gRPC for our internal SDKs, but worried about gateway complexity. What are the main telemetry gaps we expect?
leo: Telemetry gaps: distributed trace propagation, per-route token-level cost, and quota attribution. REST routes give us easy HTTP path/verb tags; gRPC needs method name extraction at layer 7 (Envoy) or adding :method metadata in x-platform headers. :thinking:
irene: For quotas we need route-level and tenant-level counters. With gRPC we can rely on service+method as keys. For REST we have to normalize paths or use operation IDs in the console. Prefer service+method (gRPC) for stable routing and less brittle rules.
maya: Can we do dual-protocol with a gateway that normalizes to a canonical operation id? i.e., REST -> x-op-id header, gRPC -> :method -> x-op-id. Then console uses x-op-id for quotas/metrics.
sam: Yes. Example Envoy config we sketched yesterday:

```
http_filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.grpc_json_transcoder
    typed_config: {"@type": "type.googleapis.com/...", "proto_descriptor": "/etc/protos/admin.pb"}
route:
  - match: {path: "/v1/users/*"}
    request_headers_to_add: [{"header": "x-op-id", "value": "users.get"}]
```

That lets us unify metrics.

leo: Note: transcoding adds CPU and edge latency. Might be fine for admin APIs (low qps) but not for latency-sensitive inference paths. We must restrict this to admin/control plane only.
irene: Rollout UX: console should show a toggle "Accept gRPC" on route config. When on, we advertise dual-stack in SDKs. Also display "mapping status" for each route — whether x-op-id present, inferred, or missing.
maya: Good. How about auth & quotas? Should quotas live at gateway (per op-id) or at service (gRPC)? Gateway-level quotas are easier for global throttling but we lose fine-grained service metrics if we only rely on gateway.
sam: I'd put primary quotas at gateway (global budget), and service-level quota checks as a secondary enforcement for tenant isolation. Gateway rejects early when global burst happens.
deploy-bot: canary v0.1 of admin-gateway deployed to staging (route-mapping enabled). Metrics pipeline: op-id -> prometheus job admin.gateway

leo: For telemetry, make sure trace ids are forwarded: x-request-id and x-cloud-trace-context, and we set resource labels op_id, tenant_id. Console debug view can show a waterfall grouped by op_id.
maya: Next steps: (1) add x-op-id header in gateway rule templates, (2) add SDK header mapping for REST clients, (3) update console route page with mapping state and quota controls, (4) run canary and verify metrics.
irene: I can take console changes. Sam/Leo pair on gateway + SDK mapper. Maya will own rollout plan. :thumbsup:
sam: Quick question — do we want to persist op-id in logs as `operation.name` so alerts and log-based metrics use the same key?
maya: Yes, persist as `operation.name` in logging schema. Add that to the rollout checklist.
maya: Thanks all — leaving this thread open for follow-ups. If anyone sees blockers ping me.
